kp.k: Freshfields reports firmwide AI adoption one year into collaboration
kp.d: In its 15 April 2026 announcement, Freshfields reports that more than 5,000 firmwide professionals use AI tools built with Google's Gemini models, one year into its strategic collaboration with Google Cloud. Artificial Lawyer repeats the firm's adoption claims rather than presenting a separate measurement.
qs: Global law firm Freshfields today announced that more than 5,000 firmwide professionals now use AI tools built with Google's Gemini models, one year into the firm’s strategic collaboration with Google Cloud.

kp.k: Gemini supports bespoke platforms for substantive legal work
kp.d: Freshfields reports integrating Gemini into internally developed platforms for due diligence, case management, multi-jurisdictional insights and general AI use. Partner and Freshfields Lab Co-Head Lukas Treichl describes Gemini as infrastructure rather than an experiment, asserting daily use by teams and clients across multiple practice areas. His commitment to expand AI's capabilities is forward-looking.
qs: Since the collaboration launched, Freshfields has integrated Google’s Gemini models across multiple bespoke legal solutions developed by the Freshfields Lab. These include Dynamic Due Diligence (D3), Case Management Platform, Multi-jurisdictional Insights Platform and the firm's proprietary general AI platform.
A year into our Google Cloud partnership, Gemini is no longer an experiment at Freshfields – it is infrastructure.
Our teams and clients use it daily across the Freshfields Lab's platforms for complex legal work spanning multiple practice areas.
As we deepen this collaboration, we will continue to expand the boundaries of what AI can deliver for our clients.

kp.k: NotebookLM adoption targets synthesis and large document sets
kp.d: Freshfields reports over 2,100 regular NotebookLM Enterprise users and describes its purpose as more efficient synthesis and navigation of complex material. The firm also reports deploying custom managed encryption keys and claims this ensures the highest level of data security; these are the firm's efficiency and security assertions.
qs: In addition, Freshfields deployed and rolled out Google NotebookLM Enterprise with CMEK (custom managed encryption keys), ensuring the highest level of data security.
Over 2,100 team members regularly use NotebookLM Enterprise to synthesize complex material and navigate large document sets more efficiently.

kp.k: Workspace embeds AI in administrative and legal workflows
kp.d: Freshfields reports rolling out Google Workspace to over 2,800 users. It identifies meeting transcription, document summarization and custom Gems for business services and legal workflows as uses of Workspace with Gemini.
qs: Freshfields has rolled out Google Workspace to over 2,800 users.
Colleagues are using Google Workspace with Gemini for meeting transcription and document summarization, and creating custom Gems for various business services and legal workflows.

kp.k: Internal training and champions underpin the adoption effort
kp.d: Freshfields describes an in-house AI Academy as integral to rollout and adoption. Its training program was supported and endorsed by leadership and partners, delivered by 260 Freshfields AI Champions, and included Google Cloud guest speakers.
qs: As an integral part of the firm’s rollout and adoption effort, Freshfields provided a comprehensive internal AI upskilling and training program, supported and endorsed by Freshfields leadership and partners.
The AI Academy was developed in-house and delivered by 260 Freshfields AI Champions, including guest speakers from Google Cloud.

kp.k: Leadership frames daily adoption as progress in client delivery
kp.d: Chief Innovation Officer Gil Perez interprets daily use, cross-team collaboration, proficiency and governance as indications that Freshfields is fulfilling its ambition to change everyday client delivery. This is leadership's assessment of the rollout, expressed as an indication of progress rather than a quantified client-service outcome.
qs: A year ago, Freshfields set out to prove that AI could genuinely change how a global law firm works in everyday client delivery,
Now, our team members use Gemini, NotebookLM Enterprise and Google Workspace daily, collaborating across teams with confidence, proficiency, and strong governance.
This is the strong indication that we are delivering on that ambition as we continue to raise the bar for our client service.

kp.k: Google frames governed integration as scalable operational AI
kp.d: Google Workspace Vice President Pat McCarthy argues that integrating Gemini with Workspace and deploying NotebookLM Enterprise moves generative AI into core business workflows. He presents the collaboration as illustrating global-scale deployment with data governance, against the legal profession's need for precise synthesis of complex information.
qs: The legal profession is defined by the need to synthesize vast amounts of complex information with absolute precision,
By integrating Gemini with Google Workspace and deploying tools like NotebookLM Enterprise, organizations like Freshfields can move generative AI out of the sandbox and into core business workflows.
This collaboration illustrates how a secure AI ecosystem can scale across a global firm while upholding essential data governance.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Freshfields reports that Gemini-based AI has become part of everyday legal delivery at firmwide scale, rather than remaining experimental.
pts.d: Freshfields' newsroom reports more than 5,000 professionals using Gemini-based tools integrated into bespoke due-diligence, case-management, multi-jurisdictional insights and general AI platforms. Chief Innovation Officer Gil Perez interprets daily use and cross-team collaboration as an indication that AI is changing client delivery and improving service. Partner and Freshfields Lab Co-Head Lukas Treichl describes Gemini as infrastructure used daily by teams and clients for complex work across practice areas. Artificial Lawyer reproduces these adoption figures and statements; they remain claims by Freshfields and its named speakers, rather than separate findings by the publication.

pts.k: Freshfields claims AI supports more efficient synthesis and document navigation, alongside transcription, summarization and customized workflows.
pts.d: The newsroom attributes more efficient handling of complex material and large document sets to NotebookLM Enterprise, regularly used by over 2,100 team members. It also reports Google Workspace rollout to over 2,800 users and describes Gemini-assisted meeting transcription, document summarization and custom Gems for legal and business-services workflows. These are reported uses and a qualitative efficiency claim, not quantified time or cost savings.

pts.k: Google's Pat McCarthy presents the collaboration as an example of secure AI scaling into core workflows; Treichl predicts further expansion of client applications.
pts.d: Google Workspace Vice President Pat McCarthy claims that integrating Gemini, Workspace and NotebookLM Enterprise allows organizations such as Freshfields to move generative AI into core business workflows while maintaining data governance. Freshfields separately claims its NotebookLM Enterprise deployment with CMEK ensures the highest level of data security. Treichl makes an open-ended prediction that deepening the collaboration will expand what AI delivers to clients, without specifying future capabilities or measurable outcomes.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered consists of firm-reported adoption counts, named deployments, training activity and executive accounts of daily use.
pts.d: Freshfields supplies counts of more than 5,000 Gemini-tool users, over 2,100 regular NotebookLM Enterprise users, over 2,800 Workspace users and 260 AI Champions delivering training. These figures describe adoption and implementation; the source does not state that the user groups are mutually exclusive. Perez and Treichl offer experience-based interpretations of operational change, while McCarthy offers a technology-partner assessment of scalability and governance. Artificial Lawyer largely repeats the firm's announcement rather than adding independent outcome evidence. No measured productivity improvement, legal-accuracy benchmark, client-outcome comparison or security test is supplied.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The reported changes are current as of 15 April 2026, one year into the collaboration; further expansion has no stated deadline.
pts.d: Both pieces are dated 15 April 2026. Adoption and integration are described as occurring over the first year of Freshfields' Google Cloud collaboration, with daily use reported by Perez and Treichl and regular NotebookLM use reported by the firm. Implementation is presented alongside bespoke platform development, leadership-supported upskilling, AI Champions, encryption-key controls and governance. These are rollout conditions described in the source, not demonstrated necessary or sufficient causes. Treichl links future expansion to deepening the collaboration but gives no specific timetable.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The described effects concern Freshfields' global professionals, legal and business-services teams, and clients receiving complex legal services.
pts.d: The principal setting is a global Magic Circle firm with a substantial US presence, as described by Artificial Lawyer. The adoption counts refer to professionals, team members or users, not exclusively lawyers. Legal teams use bespoke platforms across multiple practice areas; legal and business-services colleagues use transcription, summarization and customized workflows. Treichl includes clients among daily platform users, and Perez presents improved client service as the intended benefit. McCarthy extends the scalability claim to organizations like Freshfields. The document does not claim changes to employment levels, staffing structures, billing models or access to justice.
